UX/UI · Healthcare · Brand system

Making complex care feel clear.

A research-led experience that brings clarity and reassurance to healthcare decisions.

My roleUX/UI DesignerWork Experience
ScopeBrand strategy, UX research, landing pages, consultation flow
Tools & methodsFigma, wireframing, component systems

01 / Context & role

Support a considered healthcare decision.

The Anti-Aging Centre needed a digital experience that explained its services while communicating reassurance and credibility. My agency role connected brand strategy, research synthesis, landing-page design, and the consultation flow. I worked with brand stakeholders and frontend developers, using Figma, wireframing, and component systems.

02 / Research synthesis

Understand the questions behind the first click.

The research explored how people seek information, compare options, and decide whether to contact a centre. Treatment effectiveness, safety and side effects, cost and accessibility, reputation, and personalized care were central considerations. This decision journey informed what information the landing pages needed to make visible before asking visitors to take action.

03 / Audience & messaging

Different motivations need different emphasis.

The project focused on adults aged 30–60, with two audience segments: ages 30–45 seeking proactive approaches, and ages 45–60 interested in rejuvenation. The design response used segmented messaging within repeatable landing-page templates. This allowed the emphasis to change while preserving a familiar structure.

04 / Handwritten ideation

Connect the brand’s character to interface choices.

Early handwritten notes explored the brand’s message, emotional tone, and essential characteristics. Clarity, consistency, credibility, and audience focus became useful criteria for later visual decisions. These notes are original project artifacts that show the thinking before the polished interface.

05 / Wireframes & user flow

Build a path from introduction to consultation.

The initial click-through landing pages provided a concise introduction before directing visitors onward. The sales landing page then developed into clearly defined sections: banner, why, understanding, benefits, science, client stories, and consultation. This sequence gives each section a role in the visitor’s decision process.

06 / Interaction details

Use consistent calls to action.

Button explorations tested treatments on light and dark backgrounds, including filled and outlined directions. A shared CTA style helped connect the different landing pages. The design documentation also defines button sizing and typography, making the intended treatment easier to reproduce across layouts.

07 / Visual design & content

Balance warmth with authority.

Muted colors, calm imagery, and structured layouts formed the visual direction. Modular content blocks and simplified terminology made complex service information more approachable. Scalable page variants allowed messaging to adapt to audience needs while retaining visual continuity.

Outcome / What changed

From complex service information to a structured consultation path.

Research synthesis shaped a clear sequence from service introduction and treatment information to consultation. Modular landing-page templates let the team adapt messaging for different audiences without redesigning the page structure. Consistent CTAs and documented visual components created a repeatable interface system. The supplied project documents these delivered changes; post-launch conversion and task-completion figures are not available.

Extending the identity

One brand, across physical and digital touchpoints.

The graduation project also extends the identity into a catalog, business cards, supplement packaging, and bottle packaging. These applications connect the website’s visual language to the objects customers encounter beyond the screen.
